scope.source_policy: Current official university catalogs and official university policy, registrar, department, or college pages only.
scope.variant_policy: Model the ordinary undergraduate Computer Science B.S. without merging concentrations, other computing majors, or accelerated graduate pathways.
scope.schedule_policy: Do not use the VCU recommended sequence, VSU Plan of Study, or Virginia Tech Roadmap as requirement authority.
scope.arithmetic_policy: Preserve official gross component subtotals and documented overlap, expose every bounded menu, and use a source-explainable canonical minimum path. Never invent an upper-level, residence, or elective-submenu rule when the current catalog does not publish one.

summary.analysis_blocker_policy: All three documents pass the source-completeness and catalog-structure gate. They fail analysis_ready only because exact overlap, attribute, variable-credit, conditional-choice, or distribution rules do not yet have evaluators.

ownership.college_wide_additional_block: none published beyond ConnectED and the program requirements

official_sources.page_scope: ordinary Degree requirements container, upper-level CMSC menu, humanities subjects, natural-science routes, and 120-credit total
30-credit ConnectED foundations, breadth, inquiry-area, overlap, and prefix rules
College of Engineering and Department of Computer Science ownership, program variants, and department scope
current undergraduate graduation-policy context and graduation application authority
current CMSC course identities and credit values

major_and_degree_arithmetic.gross_overlap_finding: The program table publishes a 30-credit gross General Education requirement and marks ECON, MATH 200, and laboratory science as ConnectED-satisfying. Its displayed rows close at 120 only when those courses are represented once; the canonical composition therefore carries 21 additional ConnectED credits rather than adding 30 again.
major_and_degree_arithmetic.placement_finding: CMSC 254 appears in the displayed core but is required only when the placement test calls for it; the composition exposes either CMSC 254 or four credits of applicable degree capacity in that slot.

graduation.major_course_grade: C or better in all CSCI, MATH, and STAT courses
graduation.residency: At least 25 percent at VCU, including at least 30 of the final 45 credits.
graduation.major_course_grade: C or better in every computer science course

blockers: Focused Inquiry grade, honors eligibility, and postmatriculation transfer rules

institutions.name: Virginia State University

selected_degree.catalog_title: Computer Science Major, Bachelor of Science (B.S.)

ownership.college_wide_additional_block: none published beyond university General Education and the program Summary of Requirements

official_sources.page_scope: authoritative Summary of Requirements, fixed core and required courses, complete restricted menus, and 120-credit total
33-credit General Education distribution and complete current course menus
College of Engineering and Technology/Department of Computer Science ownership, base and concentration scope, and C-or-better CSCI/MATH/STAT rule
current undergraduate policy statements and explicit search for degree-residence and graduation minima
current academic regulations and explicit search for upper-level and degree-residence rules
current CSCI identities, titles, credits, and confirmation of CSCI 471

major_and_degree_arithmetic.restricted_pool_finding: The authoritative container publishes a single 13-credit restricted requirement followed by complete CSCI, MATH, and approved laboratory-science menus, but it does not publish how the 13 credits divide among those menus. The complete pool is exposed without importing the Plan of Study's apparent distribution.

general_education.overlap_rule: One course may satisfy General Education and the major, but one course may not satisfy two General Education areas.
general_education.science_menu_finding: The full university General Education science menu remains available for the four-credit GE category. The narrower BIOL/CHEM/PHYS list is separately exposed within the 13-credit Computer Science restricted-elective pool.

graduation.upper_division_finding: No universal bachelor's numeric minimum appears in the reviewed current sources; wording confined to the excluded Plan of Study is not promoted.
graduation.residency_finding: No numeric bachelor's degree-completion residency rule appears in the reviewed current Academic Regulations and Policy Statements; honors and admission provisions are not repurposed.
graduation.gpa_finding: No universal undergraduate graduation GPA minimum or Computer Science-specific GPA minimum appears in the reviewed current program, Academic Regulations, or Policy Statements; admission, transfer-admission, and honors thresholds are not repurposed.

institutions.catalog_conflict_resolution: CSCI 471 is in the authoritative 54-credit core and the current course dictionary. An unlabeled CSCI 470 row appears only in the excluded Plan of Study and is absent from the composition.

blockers: General Education/major overlap and single-GE-area enforcement

institutions.name: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University

selected_degree.catalog_title: Computer Science Major, Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

ownership.college_wide_additional_block: none beyond the engineering foundations embedded in Program Curriculum

official_sources.page_scope: Program Curriculum, elective rules and exclusions, substitutions, program graduation rules, and 123-credit total
Pathways authority and fall-2025 Concept 7 suspension
College of Engineering/Department of Computer Science ownership, current course identities, and complete pre-approved Career Bridge route families
25-percent institutional, final-45 transfer, two-year transfer, and GPA policies
undergraduate degree, transfer, Pathways, and acceptable-credit policy context

major_and_degree_arithmetic.elective_subtotal_reconciliation: The displayed elective rows total 29; the separately detailed eight-credit Natural Science Electives rule supplies the remaining eight and also fulfills Pathways Concept 4.
major_and_degree_arithmetic.pathways_reconciliation: 47 gross Pathways credits minus the eight natural-science credits already counted in the elective subtotal equals 39 unique credits; 24 + 15 + 8 + 37 + 39 = 123.

elective_scope.open_rules_exposed: eligible CS level rules and prior-approved capstone/non-CS technical alternatives

career_bridge.route_scope: All seven currently published pre-approved route families are exposed: full-time co-op/internship, credited or full-time research, international experience, senior Corps/ROTC leadership, qualifying client capstone, ENGE project, and approved full-time field experience; other routes remain subject to department approval.

graduation.gateway_grade_rule: C- or better in MATH 1225; C or better in CS 1114, 2104, 2114, 2505, 2506, and 3114 or approved substitutions
graduation.residency: At least 25 percent at Virginia Tech (30.75 of 123 credits, therefore at least 31 whole semester credits); no more than 18 transfer credits among the final 45; no more than 50 percent of degree requirements transferred from two-year institutions.
graduation.foreign_language: Two high-school years or one college year of the same language; college credit used solely for this rule does not count into the 123 credits.
graduation.upper_division_finding: No separate university-wide bachelor's upper-division minimum is published in the reviewed current sources.

blockers: paired honors-math substitution and free-credit adjustment
GPA, residence, transfer, and foreign-language evaluation
